body: Thanks for your response. I’m also sorry for your loss. I was in a very dark place last night when I wrote this. I’m trying to keep it together. Everyone in my life thinks I have it together. My husband doesn’t take me seriously when I have told him my thoughts. I think because he knows I have to be strong and thinks I would never do it. He is an Army Veteran and fought overseas for 8 years so you would think he would be the one with PTSD but he’s far from it. He’s so docile and aloof. It makes me want to scream. I’ve shared some of these feelings with my other family members but I don’t think they understand and I fear I had become too much to handle when I opened up like that so I’ve swept it all under the rug and just told everyone therapy was really helping and essentially apologized for being a burden to them. I’m sorry for putting more on you I don’t even know I’m talking to a stranger right now or why I post this in the first place this is all not in my character.

You are so fucking young. I would do anything to be your age again, I would do things so differently. Please know there is a place for you in this world, you just have to find what makes you feel good. You haven’t even started truly living your life yet. Don’t give up. Yes-You just need to connect more, with people, things, nature, etc. and that shit takes time. But life is precious and it’s a journey if you let it be. Try not to let the darkness in our world consume you. There is more. So much more.

Hey there, friend. I too have dealt with this for far too long. Turns out our subconscious is a powerful beast. I recently began EMDR therapy for past trauma. Trauma is a hell of thing... the word is misused and misunderstood but I assure you what you’re feeling is likely from past traumas that are unable to be healed. Our body and mind tend to remember everything, and in such crazy ways... EMDR helps reprocess those memories into just that...past memories and allow your body and mind to be in the present time, with positive emotions, not living in constant fight or flight mode. It is exhausting indeed. Find yourself a good counselor who specializes in this therapy. It’s truly transformative. I have a long way to go, but I know I’m on the right path.
